subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Toxicities of targeted agents and antibody-drug conjugates: dermatologic, metabolic, pulmonary and neurologic complications

steps.tx: Epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitors cause characteristic **acneiform papulopustular** skin eruptions on sebum-rich facial and trunk areas in up to 90% of treated patients. The proactive Lacouture protocol recommends prophylactic oral **doxycycline** or minocycline 100 mg twice daily alongside gentle alcohol-free moisturizers and topical hydrocortisone to minimize severity and prevent dose reductions.
steps.say: Epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitors cause characteristic acneiform papulopustular skin eruptions on sebum-rich facial and trunk areas in up to 90% of treated patients. The proactive Lacouture protocol recommends prophylactic oral doxycycline or minocycline 100 mg twice daily alongside gentle alcohol-free moisturizers and topical hydrocortisone to minimize severity and prevent dose reductions.

left.title: EGFR Rash Features
points: Follicular papules and pustules without comedones
Predominates on face, scalp, and upper trunk
Appears within 1 to 2 weeks of initiation
Correlates positively with antitumour efficacy

right.title: Prophylaxis and Care
points: Oral doxycycline or minocycline 100 mg BID
Topical 1% hydrocortisone cream to face
Broad-spectrum SPF 30 sunscreen daily
Avoid alcohol-containing toners and acne washes

steps.tx: **Paronychia** and pyogenic granuloma-like **periungual lesions** represent chronic, highly disabling cutaneous complications of long-term EGFR inhibitor therapy. Arising weeks to months after therapy initiation, lateral nail fold inflammation and exuberant granulation tissue produce excruciating digital pain, requiring potent topical corticosteroids, antimicrobial soaks, and partial nail avulsion.
steps.say: Paronychia and pyogenic granuloma-like periungual lesions represent chronic, highly disabling cutaneous complications of long-term EGFR inhibitor therapy. rows: Nail fold erythema and localized edema
Vinegar or chlorhexidine soaks, topical clobetasol ointment
Nail fold disruption, discharge, severe tenderness
Add oral cephalexin or clindamycin for secondary bacterial infection
Dose interruption, chemical cauterization with silver nitrate, nail avulsion

steps.tx: **Paronychia** is inflammation of the nail fold, most often from Staphylococcus aureus in acute cases. Acute infection lasting under six weeks is usually managed with warm soaks, and a discrete abscess needs incision and drainage. Chronic paronychia is typically irritant or Candida driven and is managed with antifungals and avoidance of irritants. Nail dystrophy is the commonest major complication of chronic disease.

steps.tx: **Hand-foot skin reaction** associated with multikinase VEGFR inhibitors sorafenib and regorafenib manifests as **hyperkeratotic** painful, tender blisters localized over mechanical friction and pressure points. Distinct from cytotoxic chemotherapy erythrodysesthesia, VEGFR hand-foot reaction requires preemptive hyperkeratotic callus debridement, topical urea creams, and cushioned footwear.
steps.say: Hand-foot skin reaction associated with multikinase VEGFR inhibitors sorafenib and regorafenib manifests as hyperkeratotic painful, tender blisters localized over mechanical friction pressure points. Distinct from cytotoxic chemotherapy erythrodysesthesia, VEGFR hand-foot reaction requires preemptive hyperkeratotic callus debridement, topical urea creams, and cushioned footwear.

left.title: VEGFR Hand-Foot Reaction
points: Driven by sorafenib, regorafenib, sunitinib
Hyperkeratotic, blistered, callused plaques
Confined to pressure and friction points
Managed with 10% to 20% urea cream and clobetasol

right.title: Cytotoxic Hand-Foot Syndrome
points: Driven by capecitabine, 5-FU, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin
Diffuse, symmetrical, desquamating erythema
Affects entire palmar and plantar surfaces
Managed with emollients and ice packs

steps.tx: **Trastuzumab deruxtecan** carries a major boxed warning for drug-induced **interstitial lung disease** and non-infectious pneumonitis. Because pulmonary toxicity can progress rapidly to fatal fibrosis, oncologists mandate baseline chest computed tomography, serial monitoring for cough or exertional dyspnea, immediate treatment cessation at grade 1, and prompt high-dose corticosteroid administration.

steps.tx: **Alpelisib**, an isoform-specific PI3K-alpha inhibitor, frequently induces severe grade 3 to 4 **hyperglycemia** in over 30% of treated oncology patients by disrupting insulin-stimulated cellular glucose uptake. Clinical guidelines require mandatory baseline fasting plasma glucose and glycated hemoglobin screening, accompanied by lifestyle optimization and early prophylactic metformin initiation.

rows: Initiate or escalate oral metformin 500 to 2000 mg daily
Add SGLT2 inhibitor or DPP-4 inhibitor; hold alpelisib if symptomatic
Interrupt alpelisib; administer intravenous insulin infusion and rehydrate

steps.tx: **CDK4/6 inhibitors** palbociclib, ribociclib, and abemaciclib induce uncomplicated, rapidly reversible bone marrow **neutropenia** without the true apoptotic stromal depletion typical of traditional cytotoxic chemotherapy. By inducing cytostatic G1-phase cell-cycle arrest in hematopoietic progenitors rather than cytotoxic lineage destruction, blood counts rebound rapidly during scheduled rest intervals.

left.title: CDK4/6 Inhibitor Neutropenia
points: Cytostatic, reversible G1 cell cycle arrest
Preserves stem and progenitor cell viability
Febrile neutropenia risk under 2%
Rapid count recovery within 7 drug-free days

right.title: Cytotoxic Chemotherapy Neutropenia
points: Direct DNA damage and apoptotic progenitor lysis
Extensive depletion of bone marrow precursors
Febrile neutropenia risk frequently exceeds 10-20%
Prolonged marrow recovery requiring G-CSF support

steps.tx: **Lorlatinib**, a third-generation brain-penetrant ALK inhibitor, causes unique central nervous system neurocognitive, mood, and speech adverse effects alongside profound **hypercholesterolemia** and hypertriglyceridemia in over 80% of patients. Neuropsychiatric toxicities respond to dose reduction, whereas lipid abnormalities demand aggressive lipid-lowering therapy with rosuvastatin or pitavastatin.

rows: Memory lapses, confusion, slowed speech, word finding difficulty
Dose interrupt until resolution; reduce from 100 mg to 75 mg daily
Irritability, mood swings, depression, sleep disruption
Monitor family observations; withhold and adjust dose appropriately
Baseline lipid panel; initiate rosuvastatin or atorvastatin concurrently

steps.tx: **Antibody-drug conjugates** carrying monomethyl auristatin E or deruxtecan payloads require dedicated vigilance for signature toxicities including sensorimotor **peripheral neuropathy**, ocular keratitis, and alopecia. Payloads detach inside and outside target cells, and bystander cytotoxic effects cause distinct, payload-specific systemic organ toxicities that dictate rigorous dose-modification algorithms.
